evals.name: drag-driven-continuous-haptic
evals.prompt: Implement a Swift 6.3 haptic texture whose intensity and sharpness follow a drag gesture continuously. It must stop on cancellation and recover after interruptions.
evals.expected_output: A retained Core Haptics engine and continuous player with live dynamic-parameter updates, explicit gesture cleanup, capability fallback, and reset recovery.
assertions: Checks CHHapticEngine hardware capability and preserves a non-haptic interaction path.
Creates one retained engine and installs stoppedHandler and resetHandler before starting it.
Starts one retained continuous pattern player instead of creating a new pattern for every drag update.
Uses hapticIntensityControl and hapticSharpnessControl dynamic parameters for live updates.
Stops and releases the player on gesture end and cancellation.
Recreates invalidated players after an engine reset and treats callbacks as potentially off-main-thread.
Requires verification on supported physical hardware rather than Simulator-only testing.

evals.name: designer-ahap-lifecycle-review
evals.prompt: Review an implementation that force-unwraps Success.ahap, creates CHHapticEngine inside every button action, starts it, and assumes the player survives app backgrounding. Provide a corrected architecture.
evals.expected_output: A lifecycle-safe AHAP design with a retained engine owner, checked resources, capability fallback, interruption/reset handling, and appropriate player recreation.
assertions: Rejects creating an engine per button action and assigns one clear retained owner.
Checks supportsHaptics before engine construction and keeps a fallback.
Loads the AHAP URL without force-unwrapping and handles playback errors.
Installs stoppedHandler and resetHandler before starting the engine.
Explains that reset recovery may require recreating players and registered resources.
Distinguishes direct playPattern playback from advanced-player needs such as loop, pause, seek, or callbacks.
Includes physical-device and interruption testing.

evals.name: unsupported-device-fallback
evals.prompt: Our custom confirmation waveform works on an iPhone but must also ship on iPad and Vision Pro. Design the capability and fallback behavior without making confirmation ambiguous.
evals.expected_output: Runtime capability-driven behavior that preserves semantic visual confirmation and treats haptics as enhancement rather than required state communication.
assertions: Uses capabilitiesForHardware rather than platform or device-name assumptions.
Notes that some devices including iPad and Apple Vision Pro do not support Core Haptics feedback.
Preserves the product action and clear visual state when haptics are unavailable.
Does not make audio mandatory or use haptics as the sole confirmation channel.
Separates compile/Simulator checks from physical tactile verification.

evals.name: route-standard-save-feedback
evals.prompt: Add a standard success haptic after a SwiftUI Save button completes. Should this use CHHapticEngine and an AHAP file?
evals.expected_output: A boundary-aware answer that uses SwiftUI sensoryFeedback for standard success feedback and avoids unnecessary Core Haptics lifecycle machinery.
assertions: Recommends sensoryFeedback with a state trigger for the standard SwiftUI success case.
Does not create CHHapticEngine, CHHapticPattern, or an AHAP asset for this requirement.
Routes ordinary view feedback patterns to swiftui-patterns.
Reserves Core Haptics for custom waveform, continuous, live-modulated, or synchronized audio-haptic requirements.
Keeps success visibly or semantically communicated even when haptics are unavailable.
